content.text:
I set up the project in `/work`. It has no runtime dependencies, and all 4 tests pass with `npm test`.

**How it works** (`lib/index.js`): it exports one function, `setPrototypeOf(obj, proto)`, which returns `obj`. It picks the first method the environment supports:
1. The built-in `Object.setPrototypeOf`.
2. Assigning to the `__proto__` property, for very old engines that don't have #1. It checks support with `{ __proto__: [] } instanceof Array`.
3. If neither works, it copies the prototype's properties onto the object without overwriting the object's own properties. This doesn't create a real prototype link, so `instanceof` won't work and later changes to the prototype won't show up. The README says so.

The two fallbacks are also exported as `setProtoOf` and `mixinProperties`, so the tests can check them directly in Node, which always has the built-in method.

**Files:**
- `package.json`: CommonJS, `main` and `types` set, publishes only `lib/`, and `npm test` runs Node's built-in test runner (`node --test`).
- `lib/index.js`: the code.
- `lib/index.d.ts`: TypeScript types.
- `test/index.test.js`: the 4 tests.
- `README.md` and `.gitignore`. The `.gitignore` also excludes the existing `.claude/`, `transcript.jsonl` and `*.log` files.

**Things to check:**
- **Package name:** `cross-setprototypeof` is a placeholder, so rename it before publishing.
- **Whether you need this at all:** every supported Node version and modern browser has `Object.setPrototypeOf`, so the fallbacks only matter if you target very old engines like IE ≤10. If you don't, you could call `Object.setPrototypeOf` directly or use the existing [`setprototypeof`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/setprototypeof) package, which takes the same approach.
